subject: Controlling the number and values for labels when using scale_area

messages.author: 029c9bb847a9e034
messages.subject: Controlling the number and values for labels when using scale_area
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to use the scale_area function from ggplot2 in with
qplot. This is my third day of using R, so I am going to try and
compose this question in a coherent manner. If it does not make
sense, please feel free to correct me.

I am trying to plot several distinct data points from the mpg dataset,
and one of the data points is 'displ'. My representation of 'displ'
on this plot is the size of the plot. Currently, my subset of data is
mpg$manufacturer == 'honda' in honda (e.g. honda is a dataframe
containing all the honda cars).

When I try to plot the honda data set, the honda$displ size is very
small, and I want to scale this size up with a constant, but I am not
sure how to do this. I attempted using "scale_area(to=c(3,8))"
appended to my plot definition, but I ran into two problems. First,
the scaling does not correctly map to the honda$displ values, which
are 1.6, 1.8, and 2.0. The other problemis the number of values that
show up in the legend, which turns out to be 6 (e.g. 1.638, 1.690,
...) rather than 3 (1.6, 1.8, 2.0) .

How do I control the scaling of continuous data points in a more
discrete fashion so that I only scale across 3 values rather than the
6 created by c(3, 8)? Also, how do I control the number of legend
entries in the graph after I apply the scale_area function?

Below I have included the code that I am using to form my data set,
and then create and scale my plots. I appreciate any help in advance.

-- Adam


<code>

library(ggplot2)

plot_pic <- function(base, fname, plot){
fname <- paste(base, fname, sep='')
print(plot)
pdf(fname)
print(plot)
dev.off()
}

accumulate_dataset_based_manufacturer <- function(mpg_data, mpg_brand_filter){
my_mpg_data <- NULL
for (i in 1:nrow(mpg_data)){
if (isa_brand(mpg_data[i,"manufacturer" ], mpg_brand_filter)){
my_mpg_data <- data.frame(rbind(my_mpg_data,
data.frame(mpg_data[i,])))
}
}
return (my_mpg_data)
}

isa_match <- function(data_field, allowed_datum)
{
for (d in allowed_datum){
if (data_field == d){
return (TRUE)
}
}
return (FALSE)
}

honda <- accumulate_dataset_based_manufacturer(mpg, c('honda'))

plot <- qplot(hwy, cty, data=honda, color=trans, size=displ,
geom=c("jitter")) + facet_grid( fl ~ year) +
scale_area(to=c(3,3+length(unique(honda$displ))))

print(plot)

</code>
